objective.text: Identify the layers on a transverse section through the week-3 disc.

body.general: What does a slice through the disc show? A transverse cut goes across the disc, like slicing bread, so you see it from side to side [f1]. The top of the slice is the back (dorsal), the bottom is the belly side (ventral) [f2]. On day 17, a slice through the groove at the tail end shows ectoderm on top, mesoderm in the middle and endoderm below [f3]. At the groove you can see cells dipping down into the middle [f4].
body.mbbs: A transverse section cuts across the cranial–caudal axis, so it shows the disc from left to right [f1]. Dorsal is at the top: the epiblast side, facing the amniotic cavity; ventral is the endoderm side, facing the yolk sac [f2]. A day-17 section through the primitive streak shows epiblast (future ectoderm) on top, mesoderm spreading sideways in the middle and endoderm below [f3]. At the streak, epiblast cells are caught dipping through the groove into the middle layer [f4].

facts.text: A transverse section cuts across the head–tail (cranial–caudal) axis, so it shows the disc from left to right.
Dorsal is the epiblast side, facing the amniotic cavity; ventral is the lower side, facing the yolk sac.
Through the streak on day 17, a section shows epiblast (future ectoderm) on top, mesoderm spreading in the middle and endoderm below.
At the streak, epiblast cells move down through the groove into the space between the layers.

misconceptions.wrong: A transverse section shows the head end and the tail end.
misconceptions.right: It cuts across the head–tail axis, so it shows left and right, back and belly.

misconceptions.wrong: The top of a section is the belly side.
misconceptions.right: Dorsal (the back) is the upper, epiblast side.

checks.prompt: On a transverse section through the streak on day 17, put the layers in order from dorsal to ventral.
checks.why: Dorsal is on top: epiblast, then the new mesoderm, then endoderm facing the yolk sac.

checks.prompt: Which directions can you see on a transverse section of the disc?
checks.why: A transverse cut crosses the head–tail axis, so head and tail are not in the slice.

remember.q: Which way does a transverse section cut the disc?
remember.a: Across the head–tail axis, showing left to right [f1].

remember.q: On a day-17 section through the streak, which layer is in the middle?
remember.a: Mesoderm, spreading between epiblast and endoderm [f3].
